title: Neuromorphic Computing Chips

body.text: The Von Neumann Bottleneck in Modern AI

Conventional computing architectures separate computational processing cores from memory blocks. Moving billions of weights across memory buses consumes over 80% of energy during neural network inference. Neuromorphic computing solves this crisis by mirroring biological brain topology, co-locating processing and memory within artificial spiking neurons.

items: Asynchronous Spiking Neurons: Chips compute exclusively when an event spike occurs, consuming near-zero static standby power.
Analog Memristor Synapses: Solid-state resistive RAM devices functioning as variable synaptic weights with non-volatile analog retention.
In-Memory Vector Multiplication: Executing Ohm-Kirchhoff physics operations directly across crossbar arrays in a single clock cycle.
Biological Energy Efficiency: Operating at milliwatt power budgets suitable for autonomous robotics, edge sensors, and neural prosthetics.

body.text: The human brain performs quadrillions of synaptic operations on twenty watts of power. Neuromorphic architectures emulate this evolutionary masterwork.

body.text: Spiking Neural Networks vs Deep Learning

Unlike standard backpropagation networks that compute dense continuous floating-point activations, Spiking Neural Networks (SNNs) convey temporal information through discrete microsecond-timed pulses, unlocking biological temporal pattern recognition.
